artifact.status_search_result: The known classification results on the 2-sphere (Matveev–Shevchishin and related work) describe geodesic flows superintegrable by one linear and one cubic integral, i.e. they exhibit a nontrivial degree-1 integral and concern the case without potential. No construction or nonexistence proof appears in the literature for a natural Hamiltonian system on $S^2$ with nonconstant potential that is superintegrable purely by integrals of degree $\geq 3$ and admits no nontrivial degree-1 or degree-2 integrals. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Two-dimensional superintegrable metrics with one linear and one cubic integral
status_evidence.snippet: Describes all local Riemannian metrics on surfaces whose geodesic flows are superintegrable with one linear and one cubic integral; some extend to S^2.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results on cubic superintegrability on S^2 assume a linear integral and treat geodesic flows, not natural systems with nonconstant potential and no low-degree integrals.

status_evidence.title: Superintegrability and geometry: a review of the extended Hamiltonian approach
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey of polynomial superintegrability; cubic and higher-degree cases on curved surfaces remain largely unclassified.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-degree polynomial superintegrability on curved surfaces (in particular S^2) with nonconstant potential and no quadratic/linear integrals is still an open area.
